events.title: George Washington Elected First U.S. President
events.description: The Electoral College met and unanimously elected George Washington as the first President of the United States, with John Adams receiving the second-highest number of votes and becoming Vice President.
events.significance: Established the executive leadership of the new federal government under the U.S. Constitution and set precedents for the American presidency.

events.title: Yalta Conference Begins
events.description: Franklin D. Roosevelt, Winston Churchill, and Joseph Stalin met at Yalta in Crimea to discuss the postwar reorganization of Germany and Europe as World War II neared its end.
events.significance: The agreements reached shaped postwar Europe, influenced the formation of the United Nations, and set the stage for Cold War divisions.

events.title: Ceylon Gains Independence from Britain
events.description: Ceylon, now Sri Lanka, became an independent dominion within the British Commonwealth, ending over a century of British colonial rule.
events.significance: It was part of the broader postwar wave of decolonization in Asia and marked the birth of modern Sri Lanka as a sovereign nation.

events.title: Patty Hearst Kidnapped
events.description: Newspaper heiress Patricia Hearst was abducted from her Berkeley, California apartment by the Symbionese Liberation Army, and later participated in the group's crimes.
events.significance: The case drew enormous media attention and raised lasting debates about coercion, radicalization, and criminal responsibility.

events.title: Facebook Launched
events.description: Mark Zuckerberg, with fellow Harvard students, launched Thefacebook, a social networking website initially limited to Harvard University students.
events.significance: It grew into one of the world's largest social media platforms, transforming communication, media, politics, and commerce globally.
